extracted.intended_audience: university press officers, science communicators, researchers involved in media relations, and science journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit evaluation criteria for creating university research press releases that maximize media pickup while guarding against exaggeration; focuses on timing, framing, language, multimedia, and verification practices. Emphasizes strategies used by universities and quality guardrails to avoid hype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with journal embargoes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time distribution and journalist access around journal embargoes to maximize pickup; the paper notes coordination is a common university PR strategy and part of timing the release with journal publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-language versions for international media
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide translations to reach broader international audiences; used by universities to increase visibility and media pickup across language markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher media training
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train researchers to engage effectively with media (interviews, messaging); a common institutional strategy to improve quality and responsiveness of press interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-arranged interview availability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer researchers who are prepared and available for interviews at time of release to facilitate journalist follow-up and increase likelihood of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia packages
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include images, video, b-roll, and other multimedia to make releases more attractive to journalists and distribution services; multimedia is listed as a feature of pickup-likely releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic timing around news cycles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule releases to fit broader news rhythms (avoid slow news days or compete with major events); timing is a strategic lever universities use to increase visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time release with journal publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releases that coincide with the academic paper's publication (often via embargo coordination) are more likely to be picked up; ensures relevance and timeliness for journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have clear public/applied relevance angle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame research in terms of public relevance or applications rather than purely academic interest; press releases with applied or public-facing angles are more likely to attract media attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional prestige as pickup factor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliation with a well-known or prestigious institution increases credibility and likelihood of media coverage; institutional branding and reputation drive pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accessible language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write in plain, non-technical terms to be understandable to journalists and the public; accessibility improves clarity and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer researcher for interview
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide direct access to researchers as sources to facilitate reporting and depth in coverage; availability of spokespeople increases uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a compelling narrative angle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the story with a clear, compelling narrative or hook that makes the research newsworthy and engaging to non-specialist audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate jargon
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert technical terms into everyday language; accurate translation of jargon is essential to avoid misinterpretation while remaining faithful to the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep releases short and scannable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose concise text with clear headings, bullets, and short paragraphs so journalists can quickly assess relevance; scannability increases likelihood of pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a news hook beyond academic interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Has news hook beyond academic interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an angle (timeliness, controversy, human impact) that makes the piece relevant to general news agendas, not just academic audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release writer should have scientific competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release writer should have scientific competence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure press officers or writers understand the science sufficiently to avoid misrepresentation; scientific literacy among writers is a quality guardrail against hype and error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher review before release
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have the researcher check the release for accuracy and appropriate caveats; researcher sign-off helps preserve fidelity to the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve caveats and limitations from paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Caveats and limitations preserved from paper
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include methodological limitations, uncertainty, and boundary conditions explicitly in the release so claims remain conservative and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie claims conservatively to actual findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Conservative claims tied to actual findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating implications — ensure headlines and claims directly reflect what the study demonstrates rather than extrapolating beyond evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be honest about study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Honest about study design (animal, in vitro, observational)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the type of study and its inferential limits (e.g., animal study, in vitro, observational) so readers and journalists understand generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hype and over-selection for 'sexiness'
rubrics_metrics.description: PR pressures incentivize hyping findings; volume drives selection (only catchy survives); 'sexy' topics over fundamental research; health/applied over basic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious of selection and framing biases that prioritize sensational or 'sexy' topics; strive for balanced coverage across fundamental and applied research and resist pressure to over-hype for visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure writers compensate for lack of scientific training
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release writers may not have scientific training
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where communications staff lack scientific background, implement safeguards (training, researcher review, editorial checks) to prevent inaccuracies and misinterpretation.
